name: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd
title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd - 500247 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Kotak Q2FY27 consolidated PAT rose 26% YoY to INR5,645 crore, helped by INR55,344 crore FCNR(B) mobilisation and lower credit cost of 35 bps.
summary.overview: Bank standalone PAT was INR4,212 crore, up 29% YoY, with NII up 16% YoY and cost-to-assets down to 2.40% from 2.67% a year earlier. Advances grew 25% YoY, but excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and the KMIL transferred book, growth was 19% YoY. NIM fell 22 bps QoQ to 4.31%, with 15 bps attributed to FCNR(B) and related advances. Subsidiaries contributed 26% of consolidated PAT, hit by market-linked MTM losses, and asset quality improved across gross NPA, net NPA and credit cost.

from 2.67% in Q2FY26 and 2.66% in Q1FY27

AFS MTM gains of INR10,958 crore excluded from P&L

segments.name: Corporate banking
segments.commentary: Loan book grew 25% YoY and 15% QoQ; 17% YoY and 7% QoQ excluding the KMIL transferred book. Corporate bank fee income grew 36% YoY and was 20% of Bank fee income.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: Advances grew 27% YoY and 10% QoQ to about INR1.4 lakh crore, 24% of Bank advances. Bank sanctioned INR11,200 crore under ECLGS.

segments.name: CV/CE
segments.commentary: Advances grew 8% YoY and 4% QoQ to over INR47,000 crore, 8% of Bank advances. Management says default rates are falling and collection efficiency improving.

segments.name: Unsecured retail
segments.commentary: Unsecured advances rose INR1,730 crore in Q2 vs INR707 crore in Q1, to an 8.1% share. Microcredit grew 18% YoY, personal and business loans 9% YoY, credit card portfolio 7% YoY.

segments.name: Mortgages and tractors
segments.commentary: Mortgage portfolio grew 14% YoY and 4% QoQ. Tractor loans grew 11% YoY and 3% QoQ, with management watching El Nino risk after a monsoon rainfall deficit of about 13%.

segments.name: Kotak Securities / Neo
segments.commentary: Kotak Securities PAT was INR348 crore vs INR345 crore a year earlier; account acquisitions rose 38% YoY and market share was 13.2%.

segments.name: Kotak Prime
segments.commentary: PAT of INR251 crore, up 2% YoY; customer assets grew 12% to INR47,458 crore.

segments.name: Kotak AMC
segments.commentary: PAT of INR287 crore, up 11% YoY, on average AUM of INR6,35,421 crore, up 12% YoY.

segments.name: Kotak Life
segments.commentary: Shareholders' PAT of INR198 crore; the 300% YoY jump reflects a one-time GST impact in Q2FY26. Gross written premium grew 21% YoY and AUM reached INR1.12 lakh crore, up 14%.

segments.name: KAAML (alternate assets)
segments.commentary: PAT of INR87 crore for Q2FY27; management says performance is best judged over longer periods.

guidance_outlook: Advances to grow at 1.5x to 2x nominal GDP; management says there are no liquidity or capital constraints on growth.
Remaining FCNR(B) funds (about INR55,000 crore raised, of which about INR16,100 crore lent and INR8,900 crore used for KMIL) to be deployed into customer assets over the next few quarters.
NIM to get the full-quarter FCNR(B) effect plus repo transmission on floating-rate loans from October, with full repo impact in Q4; management gave no formal margin guidance.
One-time ECL transition impact on net worth will be less than 2% of net worth; recurring credit cost impact of 12-15 bps awaits regulatory clarity expected in Q3.
Technology to stay at about 13% of total opex; acquisition and marketing costs to keep growing while manual and fixed overheads are targeted for cuts.
capex_capacity: KMIL is no longer an operating entity; its loan book (about INR9,600 crore) was transferred to the Bank after an RBI circular barring the same business in multiple legal entities.
FCNR(B) raised USD5.78 billion (INR55,344 crore), about 9.7% of the June deposit base; management calls it a one-off opportunity.
IBPC borrowings were reduced by a net INR9,800 crore during the quarter using FCNR(B) proceeds.
Repaid high-cost certificate of deposits during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Average deposits grew 19% YoY and 8% QoQ; current accounts grew 17% YoY and fixed-rate SA grew 14% YoY. Excluding FCNR(B), regular term deposits grew 15% YoY on average basis.
Core advances grew 19% YoY and 8% QoQ excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and the KMIL book; reported advances grew 25% YoY and 13% QoQ.

Non-interest income grew 23% YoY, or 17% excluding processing fee on FCNR(B)-linked advances; growth driven by FX gains, DCM syndication fees and disbursement fees. Q1FY27 included INR570 crore of subsidiary dividend income.
Loan book about 60% repo-linked and 65-70% floating; September repo-linked share was about 60%.
Kotak Neo bank-referred acquisitions grew 41% YoY and were 59% of total acquisitions. UPI issuer market share is 3.8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the P&L impact of KMIL, and how much FCNR(B) money is still left to deploy into customer assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said KMIL loans transferred in early July and their NII is booked in the Bank. KMIL's profit comes from reinvesting the cash it received, plus a standard provision release booked in the Bank. Management said remaining FCNR(B) liquidity is additive to core growth and will be deployed over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What yield or spread do the liquidity balances earn, and what is the NIM outlook for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to detail treasury yields. It said NIM should pick up as funds deploy into customer assets. It gave no margin guidance, but said repo transmission takes about three months to flow through, so Q3 should not differ significantly from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How should opex growth be thought of going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management divided opex into acquisition costs, which it wants to grow as loans and deposits grow; technology, about 13% of opex; and marketing. Fixed overheads and manual processes are targeted for cuts. No numeric opex growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time and recurring ECL impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The one-time transition impact is expected to be less than 2% of net worth. The 12-15 bps recurring credit cost increase guided earlier is pending regulatory clarity, expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is unsecured growth sustainable, and what drove the personal loan spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier personal loan volatility came from running down an inorganic StanC portfolio, which is now largely gone. Growth in cards, PL, business loans and microcredit will be granular, with the microcredit book 100% guaranteed. Management does not want to use unsecured as an acquisition tool.

risks_watch: Full-quarter FCNR(B) cost and repo pass-through will determine Q3 NIM; the pace of deploying about INR39,000 crore of FCNR(B) funds into assets is open.
Pending RBI clarity on the recurring ECL impact (12-15 bps guided) and the one-time transition hit (below 2% of net worth) on 1 April.
El Nino and a 13% monsoon rainfall deficit could hit tractor and microcredit delinquencies.
Subsidiary profits are volatile, with MTM losses on equity and debt holdings; custody balances are weak on muted FII flows.
Opex growth is likely to rise with acquisition spend, and cost-to-assets is still above some peers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core operating metrics such as credit cost, cost-to-assets, deposit franchise and subsidiary franchise, but guarded on margin and opex trajectory, where management repeatedly declined to give numeric guidance and deferred treasury yield details.
key_quotes: We believe that the FCNR(B) program is a one-off opportunity.
Our cost of fund continues to remain one of the lowest among large peers.
We really don't provide margin guidance.
KMIL will not be an operating entity going forward.

growth.why: Management guides advances to grow at 1.5x to 2x nominal GDP with no liquidity or capital constraints, backed by about INR16,100 crore of FCNR(B) funds already lent and about INR55,000 crore raised to deploy over the next few quarters; no capacity additions or margin guidance were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM fell 22 bps QoQ to 4.31% with 15 bps from FCNR(B) drag, but full-quarter FCNR(B) deployment and repo transmission from October could lift NIM; management gave no margin guidance and expects Q3 broadly similar to Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions (branches, plants) were discussed; growth is balance-sheet driven from FCNR(B) funds already raised.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides advances to grow 1.5x-2x nominal GDP with no liquidity or capital constraints; core advances grew 19% YoY ex-FCNR(B) and KMIL, and about INR39,000 crore of FCNR(B) funds remain to deploy.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital adequacy is 21.9% and management cites no capital constraints, and no new capex or capacity programme was discussed, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Advances grew 25% YoY reported and 19% core; deployment of remaining FCNR(B) funds could support upside to balance-sheet growth, though no formal numeric upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RBI clarity on the 12-15 bps recurring ECL credit cost impact is pending in Q3, and El Nino with a 13% monsoon deficit could pressure tractor and microcredit delinquencies.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Opex discipline: cost-to-assets down to 2.40%
rows.why: Cost-to-assets fell to 2.40% from 2.67% a year earlier, with technology held at about 13% of opex and fixed/manual overheads targeted for cuts, though acquisition and marketing spend will keep rising and no numeric opex guidance was given.

rows.label: RBI ECL transition and recurring credit cost clarity
rows.why: One-time transition hit guided below 2% of net worth and recurring 12-15 bps credit cost impact awaits regulatory clarity expected in Q3, with the transition effective 1 April.

rows.label: IBPC and high-cost CD repayment using FCNR(B) funds
rows.why: IBPC borrowings were cut by a net INR9,800 crore and high-cost CDs repaid during the quarter, reducing funding costs and supporting the deposit franchise.

tone.note: Management was confident on credit cost, cost-to-assets, deposit franchise and subsidiaries, but declined numeric margin and opex guidance and deferred treasury yield details; analysts pushed on NIM trajectory, FCNR(B) deployment and opex growth.

oneOffs.what: KMIL transferred loan book consolidated into Bank advances from early July; reported advances +25% YoY vs +19% excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and KMIL book

FCNR(B) mobilisation of INR55,344 crore (about 9.7% of June deposit base) creating temporary liquidity, with about INR39,000 crore still to be deployed; FCNR(B)-linked advances also flatter reported g

Kotak Life PAT up 300% YoY on a one-time GST impact in Q2FY26 base, which depresses the subsidiary base comparison; Q1FY27 also had INR570 crore subsidiary dividend income in the base for non-interest
Credit cost fell to 0.35% from 0.79% a year earlier, lifting PAT growth; the brief does not call the year-ago quarter weak or disrupted

quality.why: Core advances grew 19% YoY ex-FCNR(B) and KMIL, and average deposits 19% YoY, but reported 25% advance growth and the 26% PAT rise were lifted by temporary FCNR(B) liquidity and KMIL book consolidation, while the 0.35% credit cost (vs 0.79%) also helped PAT, and the FCNR(B) funds are not yet deployed and carry a 15 bps NIM drag.
